verdict: The recorded metric rises by 4096 bytes in all three SQL scan pairs; the traces do not establish that a specific application file or its true peak grew by 4096 bytes. H2 median rule remains unchanged.
metric: app_disk_peak_bytes = max sampled (statvfs.f_blocks - f_bfree) * f_frsize, including endpoint, minus filesystem_used_start plus initial_snapshot_allocated_bytes; sample interval 20 ms; whole filesystem, including metadata and unlinked open files

musl_identical_binary_control_scan.cross_vm_comparison: Not a paired comparison to SQL screen; different seed and fixture allocation values.

evidence_limits: Each per-file peak is independently maximized, not a simultaneous inventory. Named total is separately sampled; recursive traversal/statfs are not atomic and scan samples can miss short peaks. st_blocks uses 512-byte units, but actual allocating filesystem blocks and allocation timing are separate observations.

The SQL per-file maxima record a 4096-byte progress.json.tmp in both arms, but do not show when it overlaps the peak; this supports a possible transient auxiliary-block explanation, not attribution. Two baseline seed snapshot.prev.db per-file peaks show 4096 extra allocated bytes versus logical size, and filesystem starting occupancy is 4096 higher in the first two baseline pairs; causation is unresolved.

All six output temporary files have equal recorded peak logical and allocated bytes; endpoints have equal allocated totals. Identical peaks or endpoints do not establish identical intermediate allocation, simultaneity, or true peak. Filesystem ext4 and metadata/unlinked-file accounting can affect statvfs.
suggested_prospective_instrumentation: If a new admitted experiment needs attribution, collect timestamped paired statvfs, inode-deduplicated logical/allocated inventories including link counts and deleted-open/temp accounting at a higher bounded sampling rate and phase boundaries, retaining start/end, filesystem block-size metadata, observer overhead, control arms and immutable seeds. Quantify missed peaks and sampling overhead; do not alter historical metric or loosen gates.
